raw_case_text: A 4-year-old female child from Vizianagaram district, Andhra Pradesh, having fever for 5 days was tested positive for PF on smear examination. She was started on IV artesunate as monotherapy. She developed ascites, icterus, severe anemia, and hemoglobinuria requiring multiple blood transfusion. She was referred after 7 days of IV artesunate as she had persistent fever. At admission, her blood smear showed multiple PF. She was started on quinine and clindamycin, along with primaquine. Serial smears were obtained and parasitological clearance was documented after 4 days of therapy.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 4-year-old female child from Vizianagaram district, Andhra Pradesh, India, was referred with persistent fever, ascites, icterus, severe anemia, and hemoglobinuria after 7 days of intravenous artesunate monotherapy.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Initially diagnosed with smear-positive Plasmodium falciparum malaria after 5 days of fever, the child received 7 days of IV artesunate monotherapy at an outside facility, during which she developed persistent fever, ascites, jaundice, severe anemia requiring multiple blood transfusions, and hemoglobinuria.
subjective.past_medical_history: Resident of Vizianagaram district, Andhra Pradesh; received 7 days of IV artesunate monotherapy and multiple blood transfusions prior to referral.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for persistent fever, abdominal distension/ascites, jaundice, and dark urine (hemoglobinuria).

objective.physical_examination: Febrile, icteric, severely pale, and had clinical ascites.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Artesunate-monotherapy-refractory severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria complicated by intravascular hemolysis, hemoglobinuria, severe anemia, icterus, and ascites. Referral peripheral blood smear showed persistent multiple P. falciparum parasites after 7 days of IV artesunate. Treated with rescue quinine, clindamycin, and primaquine, achieving documented parasitological clearance on serial smears after 4 days of therapy.
